explanation: The one who lives in accordance with God's will and laws, often contrasted with the wicked.
Trust in God as the foundation for a righteous life; a firm confidence in His promises even when circumstances look dark.
Unjust actions and abuses committed by the wicked, which the prophet Habakkuk laments in his time.
This word is used metaphorically to describe how the wicked suck up other people's suffering or wealth as if it were a drink.
A container used at feasts and offerings; here it symbolizes the wicked filling themselves with violence and injustice.
This describes the wicked's unceasing hunger for power and wealth; their soul is never satisfied by God's grace, but thirsts for more violence.
Those who belong to God, are pure in heart, and live a life dedicated to His glory.
This expresses how the wicked believe they can fill their empty inner selves with material gain or power over other people.
